subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Plant roots absorb mineral ions from very dilute soil solutions by active transport because:
options: The ions must be moved against the concentration gradient into the root
The ion concentration is higher in the soil than in the root
Osmosis pulls the ions in
The ions move down their concentration gradient
questions.explain: Mineral ions are usually more concentrated inside the root, so they must be moved against the gradient by active transport.

questions.q: Why is glucose absorbed from the small intestine into the blood sometimes by active transport?
options: Glucose cannot diffuse at all
To move water into the blood
Glucose is always at a higher concentration in the gut
To absorb glucose even when its concentration is higher in the blood than the gut
questions.explain: Active transport allows glucose to be absorbed against the gradient when blood glucose is higher than in the gut.

questions.q: In an osmosis investigation, a potato chip GAINED mass. This shows the solution it was in was:
options: More concentrated than the cell contents
More dilute than the cell contents
The same concentration as the cell contents
Pure salt
questions.explain: Gaining mass means water entered by osmosis, so the surrounding solution was more dilute than the cell contents.

questions.q: In an osmosis experiment, why should the potato chips be dried with a paper towel before being reweighed?
options: To kill the cells before weighing
To remove surface liquid so only the change inside the chip is measured
To make the chips heavier
To stop osmosis happening
questions.explain: Drying removes excess surface solution so the recorded mass reflects water moving in or out of the cells, not liquid clinging to the surface.

questions.q: Which change would INCREASE the rate of diffusion?
options: A longer diffusion distance
A higher temperature
A smaller surface area
A smaller concentration gradient
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, increasing diffusion rate; larger surface area, steeper gradient and shorter distance also help.

questions.q: In osmosis, water moves from a region where it is:
options: Equally concentrated on both sides at all times
More concentrated (dilute solution) to where it is less concentrated (concentrated solution)
Less concentrated to more concentrated, using energy
More concentrated to a more concentrated solution against the gradient
questions.explain: Water moves from a dilute solution (high water concentration) to a concentrated solution (low water concentration) across a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: Why does a small cube of agar absorb a dye faster than a large cube of the same shape?
options: Diffusion does not depend on surface area
The small cube has less surface area in total
The small cube has a higher surface area to volume ratio
The large cube has a higher surface area to volume ratio
questions.explain: A smaller cube has a larger surface area relative to its volume, so substances diffuse in more quickly.

questions.q: Osmosis is the movement of:
options: Particles from high to low concentration using ATP
Water from a concentrated to a dilute solution
Any dissolved solute across a membrane
Water from a dilute to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane
questions.explain: Osmosis is the diffusion of water only, from a dilute (high water) to a more concentrated (low water) solution through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: Which of these is a passive process (needs no energy from respiration)?
options: Osmosis
Active transport of glucose in the gut
Uptake of mineral ions by roots
Reabsorption of glucose in the kidney
questions.explain: Osmosis (and diffusion) are passive; active transport requires energy.

questions.q: The leaves of plants have many stomata and air spaces. This mainly increases the rate of gas exchange by:
options: Increasing the surface area for diffusion of gases
Heating the leaf to speed up reactions
Using active transport to pull gases in
Pumping carbon dioxide against its gradient
questions.explain: Stomata and internal air spaces increase the surface area available for gases to diffuse in and out.

questions.q: Which change would slow down the rate of diffusion of a substance into a cell?
options: Increasing the diffusion distance (thicker barrier)
Increasing the surface area of the membrane
Increasing the concentration gradient
Increasing the temperature
questions.explain: A greater diffusion distance (a thicker barrier) reduces the rate of diffusion.

questions.q: Why do single-celled organisms NOT need a transport system?
options: They do not need oxygen
They have many specialised organs
They use active transport for everything
They have a large surface area to volume ratio so diffusion is sufficient
questions.explain: Their large surface area to volume ratio and short diffusion distances allow exchange by diffusion alone.

questions.q: Fish gills have many thin filaments with a very rich blood supply. The rich blood supply helps gas exchange by:
options: Providing energy for active transport of oxygen
Removing absorbed oxygen quickly to keep a steep concentration gradient
Reducing the surface area of the gills
Stopping water from entering the fish
questions.explain: A good blood supply carries oxygen away rapidly, maintaining a steep concentration gradient for diffusion.

questions.q: Animal cells placed in pure water can burst, but plant cells in pure water do not. This is because plant cells have a:
options: Strong cell wall
Cell membrane
Chloroplast
Permanent vacuole
questions.explain: The cell wall is strong and resists the pressure as water enters, stopping the plant cell bursting.

questions.q: Active transport differs from diffusion because it:
options: Requires energy from respiration to move substances against the gradient
Only moves water molecules
Moves substances down the concentration gradient
Does not require a cell membrane
questions.explain: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient and needs energy (ATP) from respiration.

questions.q: Root hair cells are well adapted for absorbing water because they:
options: Have a thick waxy layer
Carry out active transport of water
Have a large surface area and a thin cell wall
Contain many chloroplasts
questions.explain: A large surface area and thin wall maximise water uptake by osmosis (water is never moved by active transport).

questions.q: Which feature of an alveolus does NOT help gas exchange?
options: A large surface area
A thin (one-cell-thick) wall
A thick, multi-layered wall
A good blood supply
questions.explain: Alveoli have thin walls (short diffusion distance), not thick ones; thin walls speed up diffusion.

questions.q: Diffusion is best described as the movement of particles:
options: Against a concentration gradient
From a high to a low concentration down a concentration gradient
Of water only across a membrane
From a low to a high concentration using energy
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from high to low concentration, down the gradient, and is passive.

questions.q: Which process always requires energy released by respiration?
options: Osmosis of water into a cell
Evaporation of water from a leaf
Diffusion of oxygen into a cell
Active transport of ions into a root hair cell
questions.explain: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient and needs energy from respiration.

questions.q: A cell placed in a concentrated salt solution loses water and shrinks. This is because water moves:
options: Out of the cell by active transport
Into the cell by diffusion of salt
Into the cell by osmosis
Out of the cell by osmosis down its water gradient
questions.explain: The salt solution has a lower water concentration, so water leaves the cell by osmosis.

questions.q: As an organism gets larger, its surface area to volume ratio:
options: Doubles
Decreases
Increases
Stays the same
questions.explain: Larger organisms have a smaller surface area to volume ratio, so they need specialised exchange surfaces and transport systems.

questions.q: A piece of potato is placed in pure (distilled) water. What is most likely to happen to its cells?
options: Water enters the cells by osmosis and they become turgid
The cells lose mass
Water leaves the cells and they become flaccid
Sugar diffuses out of the cells
questions.explain: Pure water is more dilute than the cell contents, so water enters by osmosis, making cells turgid and increasing mass.
